classification.difficultyReason: Reuse a cosine-rule diagonal across two sine-rule lengths and a compound area calculation.

content.prompt:
A survey of a park is shown in the diagram.
A path is proposed from $B$ to $D$ and a fence is required from $B$ to $C$ to $D$.

spec.description: Quadrilateral DABC with D at top, A right, B bottom and C lower-left. Dark blue boundary; dashed black diagonal DB. Black side labels 41 m outside DA and 35 m outside AB. Interior angle arcs show 99 degrees at A, 74 degrees at C and 37 degrees between DC and DB at D. Black italic vertex labels outside the boundary.
spec.mathematics: DA=41 m, AB=35 m, angle DAB=99 degrees, angle DCB=74 degrees, angle CDB=37 degrees. The 37-degree mark is confined to triangle DCB.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the length of the path? Answer correct to the nearest metre.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Calculate the required length of fencing. Answer correct to the nearest metre.

answer.worked:
Using the unrounded value of $BD$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle CBD&=180^\circ-74^\circ-37^\circ\\\angle CBD&=69^\circ\\\frac{BC}{\sin37^\circ}&=\frac{BD}{\sin74^\circ}\\BC&=\frac{BD\sin37^\circ}{\sin74^\circ}\\\frac{CD}{\sin69^\circ}&=\frac{BD}{\sin74^\circ}\\CD&=\frac{BD\sin69^\circ}{\sin74^\circ}\\BC+CD&=\frac{BD(\sin37^\circ+\sin69^\circ)}{\sin74^\circ}\\BC+CD&\approx93\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: What is the area of the park? Answer correct to the nearest square metre.
